inline_comments.comment:
The `toHaveLiveRegion` assertion runs immediately after the second `mount()` call without wrapping in `waitFor`. The `announce()` call happens inside a `useEffect`, which runs asynchronously after the render commit. Additionally, `@react-aria/live-announcer`'s `announce()` commonly defers its DOM update via a small `setTimeout` to ensure assistive technologies detect the mutation — so the live region content may not yet be in the DOM when this assertion executes, causing intermittent failures.

Wrap each assertion in `waitFor`:
```tsx
await waitFor(() =>
  expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({ text: 'Test run started.', level: 'polite' })
);
```
The same applies to the assertions in `AnnouncesTestRunFinished` (line ~370) and `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed` (line ~398).

This import crosses package boundaries via a deep relative path (`../../../../core/src/manager/utils/toHaveLiveRegion`) rather than through a public or internal export of `@storybook/core`. Per the project's own guidelines, inter-package imports should go through the package's declared export surface. `toHaveLiveRegion` should be exported from an internal entry point (e.g., `storybook/internal/manager-utils` or similar) so callers import it as `import { toHaveLiveRegion } from 'storybook/internal/manager-utils'`.

The JSDoc comment says "string for exact match", but the implementation on line 59 uses `content.includes(text)`, which is a **substring** match, not an exact match. Either change the comment to "string for substring match" or switch the implementation to `content === text` / `content.trim() === text` to honour the documented contract. Since announcement messages are predictable strings, exact matching is usually safer to avoid false positives.

general_comments.comment: `code/addons/vitest/src/components/TestProviderRender.tsx` directly imports `announce` from `@react-aria/live-announcer` (a production runtime import — used in a `useEffect` that fires during normal Storybook UI usage), but `code/addons/vitest/package.json` does not list `@react-aria/live-announcer` as a dependency. The package is only declared in `code/core/package.json`. While Yarn workspaces hoisting may make this work at development time, it creates an undeclared peer dependency that can break in isolated or non-hoisted install scenarios. The vitest addon should declare `@react-aria/live-announcer` in its own `package.json` dependencies (or consume the functionality through a re-exported wrapper from core) so its dependency graph is self-contained.

The PR description states that `extend-to-be-announced` was added as a devDependency in `code/core/package.json` and registered in `code/.storybook/storybook.setup.ts` via `import 'extend-to-be-announced/vitest'`, and that stories use `toBeAnnounced` for assertions. In practice, neither `extend-to-be-announced` nor `toBeAnnounced` appears in the codebase — the implementation instead introduces a custom `toHaveLiveRegion` DOM-querying matcher. The description should be updated to accurately reflect what was shipped. It is also worth documenting (in code comments or the description) why a custom matcher was preferred over `extend-to-be-announced`, since the two approaches have different fidelity characteristics: `extend-to-be-announced` captures virtual announcements at the ARIA computation layer, while `toHaveLiveRegion` queries physical DOM nodes and will silently pass if the live region element is cleared before the assertion runs.
